overview: This Senate resolution designates May 10 through 16, 2026, as "National Police Week," the week that includes Peace Officers Memorial Day on May 15. It honors federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement officers and lists by name 201 officers killed in the line of duty during 2025. The resolution expresses support for officers, recognizes the need for them to have proper equipment, training, and resources, offers condolences to the families of fallen officers, and encourages Americans to observe the week. It is symbolic and does not create any program or spending. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on May 14, 2026.
for: Supporters say the resolution properly honors officers who died serving their communities and recognizes the risks law enforcement officers take.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or provide the equipment, training, or resources it says officers need.
